title: The Water Diviner
about: After the war, an Australian farmer travels to Turkey to find the sons he lost at Gallipoli.
cue: Serve the main when Joshua arrives at Ayshe's hotel in Istanbul.
faces: Black tea first, thanks. Then I cross to Gallipoli. I am not going home without my boys.

Turkish coffee with a square of lokum
Ayshe pours it slowly. Joshua learns to wait.
A tray charge applies to every order. Prices subject to change. Joshua Connor's three sons. Ayshe, the hotel owner. Form RS 1919. Images: TMDB.

    StartersAyshe's hotel meze with smoky eggplantSmoky eggplant dip, hummus, olives, feta and sumac flatbreadHow to make it2 eggplants2 tbsp tahini1 garlic clove1 lemon3 tbsp olive oil1 bunch of parsley4 flatbreads1 tsp sumac200g hummus150g kalamata olives150g fetaChar the eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill, turning, until collapsed.Cool, then scoop out the flesh.Mash with tahini, crushed garlic, lemon juice and salt.Spoon into a bowl with olive oil and parsley.Brush the flatbreads with oil mixed with sumac.Grill the flatbreads a minute each side.Serve with hummus, olives and feta.Istanbul hotel red lentil soupRed lentil soup with cumin and paprika butter, lemon and warm flatbreadHow to make it250g red lentils, rinsed1 onion, diced1 carrot, diced1 tbsp tomato paste1 L vegetable stock2 tsp ground cumin40g butter1 tsp sweet paprika1 lemon4 flatbreadsSoften the onion and carrot in half the butter for 6 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and cumin.Add the lentils and stock and simmer 20 minutes until the lentils fall apart.Blend smooth and season.Melt the rest of the butter with the paprika and drizzle over each bowl. Serve with lemon wedges and warm flatbread.Simit with white cheese and olivesOrhan carries the Australian's bag in for these.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsMajor Hasan's lamb kofteSpiced lamb skewers on flatbread with garlic yoghurt and chilli butterHow to make it600g lamb mince2 onions3 garlic cloves2 tsp ground cumin1 tsp sumac1 tsp paprika1 bunch of parsley200g Greek yoghurt3 tomatoes1 red onion1 lemon30g butter1 tsp chilli flakes4 flatbreadsMix the lamb mince with grated onion, crushed garlic, cumin, sumac, paprika, parsley and salt.Shape onto skewers.Grill, turning.Mix the yoghurt with crushed garlic.Toss the diced tomatoes and sliced red onion with parsley and lemon.Melt the butter with chilli flakes.Serve on warm flatbread with yoghurt, salad and chilli butter.Ayshe's chicken pilafRice with chicken, almonds and currants, from the hotel kitchenHow to make it600g chicken thigh fillets, diced30g butter1 onion, diced1 tsp ground cinnamon1 tsp allspice300g long grain rice600ml chicken stock40g currants40g slivered almonds, toasted1 small bunch dillRinse the rice until the water runs clear.Brown the chicken in the butter, add the onion and spices and cook until soft.Stir in the rice and currants, pour in the stock, cover and simmer on low until the rice is tender.Rest off the heat, covered, then fluff and finish with toasted almonds and dill.SweetsIstanbul pistachio and walnut baklavaLayered filo with pistachio and walnut, soaked in honey syrupHow to make it150g pistachios100g walnuts1 tsp ground cinnamon150g butter16 sheets of filo pastry200g caster sugar3 tbsp honey1 lemonBlitz the pistachios and walnuts with cinnamon until finely chopped.Brush a 20 x 30cm tin with melted butter.Layer buttered filo sheets, scatter with half the nuts, add more buttered sheets, the rest of the nuts and a final layer of filo.Cut into diamonds.Bake at 170°C.Simmer the sugar, water, honey and lemon juice into a syrup.Pour the syrup over the hot baklava and leave to soak and cool.Gallipoli Anzac biscuitsChewy oat, coconut and golden syrup biscuitsHow to make it100g rolled oats150g plain flour80g desiccated coconut120g brown sugar125g butter2 tbsp golden syrup1 tsp bicarbonate of sodaMix the oats, flour, coconut and brown sugar.Melt the butter with golden syrup, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda dissolved in a splash of boiling water so it foams.Pour into the dry mix and stir well.Roll into balls and flatten slightly on lined trays, leaving room to spread.Bake at 170°C until golden.Cool on
